# Wisdom of Solomon Chapter 6 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Wisdom 6 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/WIS_006_page_001.jpg

---

**6:1** Listen, kings. Understand. Pay attention, you who judge the farthest corners of the earth.

**6:2** Hear this, all who hold authority over many people, who pride themselves on commanding many nations.

**6:3** The authority you hold was given to you by the Lord. Your sovereignty comes from the Most High. And he will examine what you have done with it. He will probe your intentions.

**6:4** You were servants of his kingdom — but you did not judge rightly. You did not uphold the law. You did not walk in the direction God intended.

**6:5** He will come down on you suddenly and terribly. Severe judgment waits for those who occupy the high places.

**6:6** The person of no standing may be forgiven in mercy. But the powerful will face a powerful reckoning.

**6:7** The Lord of all is not swayed by anyone's status. Greatness does not impress him. He made both the small and the great. He holds them all in equal care.

**6:8** But those who exercise power will be subjected to a rigorous examination.

**6:9** So these words of mine are addressed to you — you who rule. Learn wisdom. Stop transgressing.

**6:10** Those who kept what is holy in a holy way will themselves be made holy. Those who received instruction will find they have a solid defense.

**6:11** So — desire my words. Hunger for them. And you will be taught.

**6:12** Wisdom is luminous and never fades. She makes herself accessible to everyone who loves her; she lets herself be found by everyone who seeks.

**6:13** She is in a hurry to be known by those who want her.

**6:14** The one who wakes up early to seek her will have no struggle. He will find her already there, sitting at his door.

**6:15** Keeping her in mind is perfect understanding. The one who lies awake thinking of her will quickly reach the point where he has nothing left to worry about.

**6:16** Because wisdom herself goes out looking for those who are worthy of her. She meets them, full of grace, on their way. In every searching thought, she comes to them first.

**6:17** The first step toward wisdom is a genuine desire to be taught. Caring about instruction is already loving her.

**6:18** Loving her means keeping her laws. Keeping her laws is the guarantee of imperishability.

**6:19** And imperishability brings a person close to God.

**6:20** So: desire wisdom, and you are on the road to a kingdom.

**6:21** If thrones and scepters are what you love, O rulers — then honor wisdom. Honor her, and you will reign forever.

**6:22** What wisdom is, and how she came into being — I will tell you all of it. I will hide nothing from you. I will trace her from the very beginning of creation. I will bring knowledge of her into the open. I will not bypass the truth.

**6:23** I will not be twisted by envy in the telling — because a person twisted by envy has no place alongside wisdom.

**6:24** The flourishing of the world depends on having many wise people in it. A ruler with good judgment is the bedrock of stability for those under him.

**6:25** So — take instruction from what I say. You will be the better for it.

---

*PNEUMA notes: The address to kings is given a direct, almost urgent quality — these are people who think they are too powerful to need instruction. Wisdom's active seeking (vv. 13–16) is emphasized through the motion verbs. The sorites (vv. 17–20) is rendered in short steps so the logical chain is visible. Verse 23's envy echo with 2:24 (the devil's envy) is preserved through the language of "twisted by envy."*
